title: From one hormone to many glucose molecules
caption: Adrenaline never enters the liver cell: it binds a receptor in the membrane, and the cell makes its own second messenger, cyclic AMP. Each step activates many molecules of the next, so a few hormone molecules release vast numbers of glucose molecules.
alt: Seven boxes in order: adrenaline, a G-protein-coupled receptor, adenylyl cyclase, cyclic AMP, protein kinase A, a chain of enzymes, and glucose released from glycogen.
description: Adrenaline: first messenger: stays outside the cell.
G-protein-coupled receptor: in the membrane: the hormone binds.
Adenylyl cyclase: switched on inside the membrane.
Cyclic AMP: second messenger, made inside the cell.
Protein kinase A: activated by cAMP.
Chain of enzymes: each activates many of the next.
Glucose: released from glycogen in the liver.
